data.name: Poland
data.summary: Poland taxes capital gains and dividends at a flat 19%, with a 4% solidarity levy on income above PLN 1m that hits large capital gains (23%) but not dividends. Gifts and inheritances to children are exempt if reported within 6 months. No wealth tax. New arrivals can opt for a PLN 200,000 a year lump sum on all foreign income for 10 years (PLN 100,000 per family member, plus PLN 100,000 a year of required qualifying spending).

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Flat 19% on capital income, 4% solidarity levy above PLN 1m (gains, not dividends).
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident with centre of vital interests in Poland or more than 183 days in a tax year.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares, bonds, fund units and company stakes are taxed at a flat 19% ('Belka' tax, art. 30b PIT Act), with no holding-period exemption. These gains count toward the 4% solidarity levy on combined income above PLN 1,000,000 a year (art. 30h), so the marginal rate on a large gain is 23%. Real estate sold more than 5 years after the end of the year of purchase is exempt; otherwise 19% (not subject to the levy).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Solidarity levy threshold: PLN 1,000,000 of combined income taxed under art. 27 (scale), 30b (capital gains), 30c (flat business) and 30f (CFC). Real estate: 5-year rule (counted from the end of the calendar year of acquisition).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Exit tax applies to unrealised gains when moving assets or residence abroad (PwC). Gains on Polish real estate companies and Polish shares are Polish-source even for non-residents.

capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation; foreign tax credited up to the Polish tax.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at a flat 19% (art. 30a), withheld for Polish companies and self-assessed for foreign dividends with a credit for foreign tax up to 19%. Dividends are NOT in the base of the 4% solidarity levy.

dividends.withholding_outbound: 19% on dividends paid to residents and non-residents, reduced by treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption.
dividends.treaty_network: About 87 treaties in force (PwC list of 92, 5 not yet in force), including the US.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Polish CIT 19% (9% small taxpayers). Distribution to an individual bears 19%. A Polish family foundation (fundacja rodzinna, since 2023) is CIT-exempt on its ongoing passive activity (PwC); distributions are taxed separately (not researched here).

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax or net worth tax.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift tax exists, but transfers to the 'zero group' (spouse, descendants, ascendants, stepchildren, siblings, stepparents) are fully exempt provided the acquisition is reported to the tax office within 6 months (for inheritance, from the court ruling becoming final or registration of the notarial certificate of succession). Cash gifts above the tax-free amount must also be received by bank transfer. If the conditions are missed, Group I rates of 3-7% apply.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Zero group exemption unlimited if reported (art. 4a). No reporting needed for acquisitions within the Group I tax-free amount, or when made by notarial deed.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: Notification (form SD-Z2) within 6 months; cash gifts documented by transfer to the recipient's account.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Failure to report: taxed as Group I (3% / 5% / 7% above the tax-free amount, aggregating 5 years of transfers from the same person). Gifts invoked only during a tax audit: 20%.

inheritance.business_relief: Not needed for children under the zero group exemption.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Polish-situs assets are always in scope (except movables and rights where neither party is Polish citizen or resident); foreign assets are in scope if the heir/donee is a Polish citizen or has permanent residence in Poland (art. 2).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Scope follows the recipient's Polish citizenship or permanent residence at the time of acquisition.

regimes.name: Lump-sum tax on foreign income (ryczałt od przychodów zagranicznych, art. 30j-30p)
regimes.description: Fixed annual tax of PLN 200,000 replacing PIT on all foreign-source revenue (except CFC income) for up to 10 years; spouse and children can join at PLN 100,000 each.
regimes.eligibility: Not Polish-resident in at least 5 of the 6 tax years before the move; elect by end of January of the year after the move with a residence certificate; spend at least PLN 100,000 a year on qualifying public-benefit purposes (economic growth, science, education, culture, sport) from the year after the move. Rights lost if the lump sum is unpaid, the spending is missed, or residence moves abroad.

lump_sum.notes: PLN 200,000 for the main taxpayer (pro rata in the arrival year) plus PLN 100,000 per electing family member (spouse, child) with no spending duty for them; plus the main taxpayer's PLN 100,000 minimum annual qualifying spending. Family of five electing: PLN 600,000 + PLN 100,000 spending. Polish-source income taxed normally.

capital_gains.summary: Under the lump-sum regime, foreign-source income including gains on foreign securities and foreign real estate is covered by the fixed annual PLN 200,000 and not taxed further. Polish-source gains stay under the normal 19% (+4%) rules.

regimes.name: Family foundation (fundacja rodzinna)
regimes.description: Since 22 May 2023 a Polish family foundation can hold the family's portfolio. Its income from permitted activity, which includes holding and trading shares and financial instruments, is exempt from CIT, so gains and dividends are untaxed while they stay inside. Benefits paid to beneficiaries are taxed at 15% CIT payable by the foundation; the founder's spouse, children and other close relatives are exempt from PIT on them. No inheritance event arises when the parents die (children already inherit tax-free in Poland if the transfer is reported). A Ministry of Finance project of August 2026 would raise the 15% to 19%, add a 36-month holding period and CFC rules from 2027 at the earliest; not law, a similar 2025 bill was vetoed.
regimes.eligibility: Founded by a natural person by notarial deed or will and entered in the register of family foundations; founding capital at least PLN 100,000 (stays in the foundation). The founder and their close family can be beneficiaries.
regimes.duration_note: A holding vehicle has no statutory time limit; it lasts as long as the family keeps it and stays resident, subject to changes in the law. Proposed 2027 changes (19% rate, 36-month holding) would change its terms, not end it.

structure.entity: Fundacja rodzinna (family foundation, Act of 26 January 2023)
structure.payout_notes: The foundation pays 15% CIT on the value of benefits (świadczenia) transferred to beneficiaries, on assets distributed at dissolution (base reduced by the tax value of what the founder contributed) and on hidden profits (art. 24q CIT Act). Beneficiaries who are the founder's spouse, descendants, ascendants, stepchildren, siblings or step-parents are exempt from PIT on benefits; tax groups I-II pay 10% PIT and others 15% (Grant Thornton). For this family the payout tax is therefore 15%, borne by the foundation. Proposed (not law): 19% from 2027 at the earliest.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: The CIT exemption covers only the permitted activities of the foundation act (holding shares and financial instruments, trading them, selling assets not bought solely for resale, renting to unrelated parties, lending to beneficiaries/companies it holds); any other activity is taxed at 25%. Renting property to a related party for its business is taxed at 19% (creditable against the 15%). Hidden profits (e.g. non-arm's-length deals with beneficiaries) taxed at 15%. Minimum tax on buildings applies. General anti-abuse clause. Not currently subject to CFC rules and no minimum holding period before selling contributed assets (Grant Thornton, August 2026). Foreign withholding tax is not creditable because the foundation pays no CIT on the income. Running and setup costs are estimates (board, accounting and financial statements, notary and registry fees); no official figure was found.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: The foundation is a separate legal person: beneficiaries who emigrate do not take its assets with them, and the individual exit tax (on personal assets above PLN 4m) does not reach foundation assets (not verified). On dissolution, distributed property bears 15% CIT, with the base reduced by the founder's contributed value.

income.name: Poland

income_tax.summary: Resident income tax is 12% on income up to PLN 120,000 (tax-free amount PLN 30,000, delivered as a PLN 3,600 tax-reducing amount) and PLN 10,800 plus 32% above that; a 4% solidarity levy applies above PLN 1,000,000. Employee contributions: 13.71% (pension and disability 11.26% up to the PLN 282,600 annual cap, sickness 2.45% uncapped) plus 9% health on income net of those contributions, uncapped. The recorded rate is the combined 22.71%; the cap applies to the 11.26% pension and disability part only.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Derived approximate rate on an income of about EUR 54,000 (about PLN 230,000 at an assumed ~4.25 PLN/EUR): fixed ZUS social contributions of PLN 1,870.24 a month (lower end, PLN 22,443 a year) plus 9% health on the tax scale (about PLN 18,700) is roughly PLN 41,100, i.e. about 17.9%. The fixed ZUS part does not scale with income; at EUR 130,000 (about PLN 550,000) the same components give roughly 12-13%. Statutory ZUS social contributions on the minimum base of PLN 5,652 a month are PLN 1,870.24-2,020.58 a month depending on the accident rate (33.09% of the base at the lower end). The pension and disability cap does not change the fixed base. Health, included in the recorded rate at the scale option: 9% of income (min PLN 432.54 a month from Feb 2026) on the tax scale, 4.9% of income on the 19% flat tax, and a fixed amount on ryczalt by annual revenue (PLN 498.35 to 60,000; 830.58 for 60,000-300,000; 1,495.04 above 300,000 on the PwC 2023 labels, which equal the 2026 figures quoted by a secondary source). A preferential ZUS on a PLN 1,441.80 base (PLN 441.76-480.11 a month) is available to new businesses. Business income: flat 19%, 14% for certain professions and 12% for designated IT services on lump-sum basis.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax in the sources opened; the page does not cover local taxes. The 0% bracket from 0 to 30,000 stands in for the tax-free amount, so personal_allowance is 0.
